selections.rationale: First pass on the EPaxos replica. Traced both core lines (A1 qualified support for decision formation; A2 per-instance ballot/authority transitions) plus the A3 recovery, A5 execution, A6 persistence and A7 client paths that connect them, and wrote a usable partial map in map.json. Formation: handlePropose allocates an own-row instance, startPhase1 pre-accepts with conflict-derived (seq,deps), and handlePreAcceptReply fast-commits on an agreeing fast quorum on the initial ballot (COMMITTED) or falls back to Accept needing a majority. Context/authority: authority is per instance via bal/vbal; acceptors reject lower ballots, makeBallot raises the ballot, and recovery issues Prepare then either accept-commits, try-pre-accepts, or restarts phase1 from the highest-VBallot replies. Connection: recovery rebuilds the same F-PREACCEPT-STATE facts the formation path consumes, CommittedUpTo exposes a stable committed prefix, and execution consumes only the committed dependency graph, so old client proposals are carried through lb.clientProposals and re-proposed on a NOOP commit. Several local anomalies were recorded as sourced unknowns rather than defects: the handlePreAccept Status>=ACCEPTED & Cmds==nil branch writes InstanceSpace[LeaderId] instead of the instance being handled; the subcase-3 and subcase-4 guards in handlePrepareReply are textually identical; and the notInQuorum loop in handleTryPreAcceptReply indexes possibleQuorum[tpar.AcceptorId] instead of possibleQuorum[q]. feedback.answered: Core relationships recorded. formation.explanation: A coordinator pre-accepts a batch in its own row (B-PROPOSE/B-PHASE1), then aggregates PreAcceptReply: if the fast quorum agrees on seq/deps (allEqual), the trial ballot is the initial ballot, and (for N>7) all committed deps are present, it fast-commits; otherwise it enters Accept and needs a majority. Both paths produce a concrete per-instance (Cmds, Seq, Deps) recorded as F-DECISION/F-COMMITTED and propagated by Commit.

context.explanation: Authority is per instance, carried by bal/vbal (F-BALLOT). A coordinator acquires the trial ballot in startPhase1; acceptors only accept a ballot >= their stored bal, so a higher-ballot message transfers authority away from a stalled coordinator. Recovery (A3) raises the ballot via makeBallot, issues Prepare, and reconstructs the instance's (vbal, status, seq, deps) from a slow quorum, then re-uses the formation paths. Established COMMITTED instances are not re-decided (handleCommit returns early), and CommittedUpTo exposes a stable committed prefix to acceptors and coordinators.

connection.explanation: Recovery and formation share the same per-instance facts: a recovering coordinator rebuilds F-PREACCEPT-STATE from the highest-VBallot Prepare replies and then either takes the slow Accept path, TryPreAccept (guarded by findPreAcceptConflicts), or restarts phase1 with a NOOP/old command. Committed support is the boundary: acceptors report CommittedUpTo, handleCommit is idempotent for already-COMMITTED instances, and execution (B-EXEC) consumes only the committed dependency graph. Thus old requests survive via lb.clientProposals carried into recovery and re-proposed on a NOOP commit, and established decisions constrain all later formation by fixing (Cmds, Seq, Deps) and the contiguous committed prefix.

open_details: CommittedUpTo is reported as PreAcceptReply.CommittedDeps and merged only when N>7; for smaller N the coordinator relies on local CommittedUpTo. Whether this is sufficient is a local question, not a formation gap.

findPreAcceptConflicts iterates from ExecedUpTo[row] (not +1); whether an already-executed instance can be misclassified as a conflict is a local anomaly.

Committed support is the boundary: acceptors report CommittedUpTo, handleCommit is idempotent for already-COMMITTED instances, and execution (B-EXEC) consumes only the committed dependency graph. The gap itself is real and now recorded in the map: a higher-ballot AcceptReply is dropped at the equality gate (epaxos/epaxos.go:1024-1026) so handleAcceptReply never counts a nack or calls makeBallot/bcastPrepare. But non-completion at a ballot is not final for the instance. Every replica's executeCommands loop re-examines each row from ExecedUpTo+1 and, when a head instance stays non-executable for COMMIT_GRACE_PERIOD, enqueues instancesToRecover for that instance (epaxos/epaxos.go:385-435); the local loop then runs startRecoveryForInstance, which rebuilds the instance bookkeeping and calls makeBallot then bcastPrepare (epaxos/epaxos.go:1127-1169). makeBallot chooses the recovering replica's own ballot slot, and for a replica that is not the row owner it uses r.Id + N, while an IsLeader additionally raises past maxRecvBallot (epaxos/epaxos.go:439-451), so a recovery attempt at an equal-or-higher ballot is available without the Accept-path escalation.
